reason: The wheels need support on loose sand, so combining the metal stock and cargo mesh seems like a way to make a crossing surface.
expectation: I expect some kind of traction mat or support for the drift, though I don't know exactly what it will make.

alternatives.reason: Anchoring the winch might help move the rover, but the immediate goal is to support its wheels.

effect: The panels provide a way to spread the wheels' weight and give the treads grip across the drift.
reaction: It is satisfying that the metal and mesh made a crossing suited to the short patch.
reason: Placing the panels on the soft drift should prepare the supported crossing the goal calls for.
expectation: I expect the panels to be laid across the loose ground so the rover can cross, though the winch may still be needed.

alternatives.reason: Anchoring the winch could help move the rover, but the panels seem like the direct next step for supporting its wheels.

effect: The panels now support the wheel tracks up to the rock lip, so the remaining task is to bring the rover across.
reaction: The explanation of how the panels prevent narrow ruts makes the crossing feel practical.
reason: Anchoring the winch is the only offered combination and seems useful for pulling the rover toward firm ground.
expectation: I expect the winch to attach to the rock anchor and help move the rover onto the lip, though another step may be needed.

effect: The winch is anchored and aligned with the panels, ready to steady the rover across them.
reaction: The aligned pull makes the recovery setup feel coherent.
reason: Combining the recovery line with the crossing is the only offered combination and seems like the next step toward the firm lip.
expectation: I expect the rover to move across the panels onto firm ground, steadied by the winch.

effect: The rover reached the firm rock lip with the cold case still secured, completing the crossing and bringing the ice face within reach.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the panels and winch work together as intended.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the traction panels was most worthwhile: the explanation connected their broad crosspieces and mesh to spreading wheel load and providing grip.

leastWorthwhile.text: Anchoring the winch and then combining the line with the crossing felt somewhat sequential, though both steps had a clear purpose.

surprise.text: I had expected the winch to pull the rover across, but learned that its steadying pull worked alongside the panels spreading the wheel load.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary; each part of the recovery setup had an explained role.

continue.text: Yes. Reaching the ice face with the cold case makes me curious about collecting the second core and what it might reveal.
